title: Choosing a PRIO-GRID conversion workflow
text: detailed guides available :
code: vignette("pg_from_points", package = "priogridR") vignette("pg_from_raster", package = "priogridR") vignette("pg_from_vector", package = "priogridR") vignette("pg_from_netcdf", package = "priogridR") vignette("pg_from_table", package = "priogridR")

title: Choosing a PRIO-GRID conversion workflow
text: small configuration useful examples exploratory work: Use default priogrid::pg_current_config() official global half-degree grid required.
code: config <- priogrid::pg_config(   nrow = 18,   ncol = 36,   temporal_resolution = "1 year",   start_date = as.Date("2020-12-31"),   end_date = as.Date("2022-12-31"),   verbose = FALSE )

title: Choosing a PRIO-GRID conversion workflow
text: Every converter accepts return argument: return = "data" returns cell-level data frame; return = "raster" returns terra::SpatRaster; return = "result" returns pg_result containing data, raster, conversion metadata. default "data". Use pg_write_result() save tabular raster outputs, pass filename directly converter.

title: Choosing a PRIO-GRID conversion workflow
text: Check coordinate reference system conversion, distinguish missing values meaningful zeros, choose aggregation rule matches meaning source variable. particular, totals generally require different transfer rule rates, proportions, categories.

title: Getting started with priogridR
text: PRIO-GRID identifiers start south-western cell increase eastward, northward. matrix returned pg_create_indices() displayed northernmost row first:

title: Getting started with priogridR
text: pg_neighbors() returns queen-contiguity neighbors: cells sharing edge corner. Longitude wraps across antimeridian default, latitude wrap across poles. grid wrap longitudinally, use:
code: pg_neighbors(5, nrow = 3, ncol = 3) #> [1] 7 8 9 4 6 1 2 3 pg_neighbors(1, nrow = 3, ncol = 3) #> [1] 6 4 5 3 2 pg_neighbors(   1,   nrow = 3,   ncol = 3,   wrap_longitude = FALSE ) #> [1] 4 5 2

title: Getting started with priogridR
text: pg_paths() constructs conventional project paths without changing working directory: Pass create = TRUE directories created.
code: pg_paths(root = tempdir()) #> $root #> [1] "/tmp/Rtmp127sMi" #>  #> $raw #> [1] "/tmp/Rtmp127sMi/data/raw" #>  #> $processed #> [1] "/tmp/Rtmp127sMi/data/processed" #>  #> $temporary #> [1] "/tmp/Rtmp127sMi/data/temp"

title: Getting started with priogridR
text: Conversion functions can return: data frame return = "data"; terra::SpatRaster return = "raster"; pg_result containing data, raster, metadata return = "result". Use pg_write_result() save supported tabular raster outputs. See conversion-workflows vignette format-specific examples.

title: Getting started with priogridR
text: pg_theme() supplies minimal map-oriented ggplot2 theme:
code: ggplot2::ggplot(   mtcars,   ggplot2::aes(x = hp, y = mpg) ) +   ggplot2::geom_point() +   pg_theme()

title: Converting NetCDF data
text: Using SpatRaster makes example independent platform-specific NetCDF drivers exercising complete conversion path. Supply explicit dates object contain reliable time metadata:
code: config <- priogrid::pg_config(   nrow = 18,   ncol = 36,   temporal_resolution = "1 year",   start_date = as.Date("2020-12-31"),   end_date = as.Date("2021-12-31"),   verbose = FALSE )  precipitation <- terra::rast(   nrows = 18,   ncols = 36,   nlyrs = 2,   xmin = -180,   xmax = 180,   ymin = -90,   ymax = 90,   crs = "EPSG:4326" ) terra::values(precipitation) <- cbind(   rep(10, terra::ncell(precipitation)),   rep(12, terra::ncell(precipitation)) ) precipitation_pg <- pg_from_netcdf(   x = precipitation,   variable = "precipitation",   aggregation = "mean",   time = c(2020, 2021),   config = config )  head(precipitation_pg)

title: Converting NetCDF data
text: file contains one main variable, pass path directly: files multiple subdatasets, identify required one source_variable: Inspect available subdatasets terra::sds() file metadata choosing source_variable.
code: precipitation_pg <- pg_from_netcdf(   x = "data/raw/precipitation.nc",   variable = "precipitation",   aggregation = "mean",   config = config ) temperature_pg <- pg_from_netcdf(   x = "data/raw/climate.nc",   source_variable = "temperature",   variable = "temperature",   aggregation = "mean",   layer = 1:12,   config = config )

title: Converting NetCDF data
text: valid time metadata present, function uses automatically. Otherwise, supply one time value per selected layer. layer argument can select layers position name time validation. Use na_values encoded missing values: Choose aggregation disaggregation rules according whether variable continuous, cumulative, categorical. See vignette("pg_from_raster", package = "priogridR") detailed guidance.
code: precipitation_pg <- pg_from_netcdf(   x = "data/raw/precipitation.nc",   variable = "precipitation",   aggregation = "mean",   na_values = c(-9999, 9.96921e+36),   config = config )

title: Converting point and event data
code: events <- data.frame(   longitude = c(10.1, 10.4, 20.2, 20.4),   latitude = c(50.1, 50.4, 60.2, 60.4),   event_date = as.Date(c(     "2020-03-01", "2020-07-15", "2021-02-01", "2021-09-10"   )),   fatalities = c(2, 3, 1, 4),   event_type = c("A", "A", "B", "B") )  config <- priogrid::pg_config(   nrow = 18,   ncol = 36,   temporal_resolution = "1 year",   start_date = as.Date("2020-12-31"),   end_date = as.Date("2021-12-31"),   verbose = FALSE )

title: Converting point and event data
text: Specify coordinate columns x data frame. Coordinates assumed use EPSG:4326 unless input_crs says otherwise.
code: event_counts <- pg_from_points(   x = events,   variable = "event_count",   longitude = "longitude",   latitude = "latitude",   aggregation = "count",   time_column = "event_date",   config = config )  event_counts #>   pgid measurement_date event_count #> 1  524       2020-12-31           2 #> 2  561       2021-12-31           2

title: Converting point and event data
text: sum, mean, min, max rules require value column.
code: fatality_totals <- pg_from_points(   x = events,   variable = "fatalities",   longitude = "longitude",   latitude = "latitude",   value = "fatalities",   aggregation = "sum",   time_column = "event_date",   config = config )  fatality_totals #>   pgid measurement_date fatalities #> 1  524       2020-12-31          5 #> 2  561       2021-12-31          5

title: Converting point and event data
text: Use group_columns retain separate summaries, example event type. Grouped results support return = "data" . keep_empty = TRUE, unobserved cells receive zero count, presence, sum. Missing means, minima, maxima remain missing zero different substantive meaning.
code: counts_by_type <- pg_from_points(   x = events,   variable = "event_count",   longitude = "longitude",   latitude = "latitude",   aggregation = "count",   group_columns = "event_type",   config = config )

title: Converting point and event data
text: x already sf SpatVector point object, omit longitude, latitude, input_crs. Set return = "result" tabular raster representations plus metadata useful. See vignette("pg_from_vector", package = "priogridR") mixed vector workflows involving lines polygons.
code: result <- pg_from_points(   events,   variable = "event_count",   longitude = "longitude",   latitude = "latitude",   aggregation = "count",   return = "result",   config = config )  pg_write_result(result, "event_counts.csv")

title: Converting raster data
text: Convert raster request tabular output:
code: config <- priogrid::pg_config(   nrow = 18,   ncol = 36,   start_date = as.Date("2020-12-31"),   end_date = as.Date("2021-12-31"),   verbose = FALSE )  temperature <- terra::rast(   nrows = 18,   ncols = 36,   xmin = -180,   xmax = 180,   ymin = -90,   ymax = 90,   crs = "EPSG:4326" ) terra::values(temperature) <- seq_len(terra::ncell(temperature)) / 10 temperature_pg <- pg_from_raster(   x = temperature,   variable = "temperature",   aggregation = "mean",   return = "data",   config = config )  head(temperature_pg)

title: Converting raster data
text: Available rules sum, mean, min, max, median, modal. Choose rule based variable’s meaning: use mean continuous surfaces temperature; use sum quantities accumulate across source cells; use modal categorical rasters; use minima, maxima, medians summaries answer research question. source raster coarser target grid, disagg_method controls interpolation. Nearest-neighbor interpolation appropriate categories, bilinear cubic interpolation may suit continuous data.

title: Converting raster data
text: Multi-layer rasters require one date year per layer unless dates handled pg_from_netcdf(). Use layer select subset conversion na_values translate source sentinel values, -9999, NA.
code: temperature_series <- c(temperature, temperature + 1)  temperature_time <- pg_from_raster(   x = temperature_series,   variable = "temperature",   aggregation = "mean",   time = c(2020, 2021),   config = config )  head(temperature_time)

title: Converting raster data
text: NetCDF variables automatic layer-time extraction, see vignette("pg_from_netcdf", package = "priogridR").
code: result <- pg_from_raster(   x = temperature,   variable = "temperature",   aggregation = "mean",   return = "result",   config = config )  result pg_write_result(result, "temperature.csv") pg_write_result(result, "temperature.tif")

title: Converting geographically indexed tables
text: source_id identifies rows table, geography_id identifies matching polygons.
code: make_rectangle <- function(xmin, xmax, ymin, ymax) {   sf::st_polygon(list(matrix(     c(       xmin, ymin,       xmax, ymin,       xmax, ymax,       xmin, ymax,       xmin, ymin     ),     ncol = 2,     byrow = TRUE   ))) }  districts <- sf::st_sf(   district_id = c("A", "B"),   geometry = sf::st_sfc(     make_rectangle(5, 15, 45, 55),     make_rectangle(15, 25, 45, 55),     crs = 4326   ) )  population <- data.frame(   district_id = c("A", "B"),   population_total = c(100000, 150000) )  config <- priogrid::pg_config(   nrow = 18,   ncol = 36,   start_date = as.Date("2020-12-31"),   end_date = as.Date("2021-12-31"),   verbose = FALSE ) population_pg <- pg_from_table(   x = population,   variable = "population",   value = "population_total",   geography = districts,   source_id = "district_id",   geography_id = "district_id",   aggregation = "area_weighted_sum",   config = config )  head(population_pg) #>   pgid population #> 1  487   26308.96 #> 2  488   65772.40 #> 3  489   39463.44 #> 4  523   23691.04 #> 5  524   59227.60 #> 6  525   35536.56

title: Converting geographically indexed tables
text: Three rules available: area_weighted_sum allocates source-unit total proportion polygon overlap cell. appropriate totals population uniform spatial distribution acceptable assumption. area_weighted_mean weights source values overlap area target cell. suitable rates continuous attributes. constant assigns source value without proportional allocation appropriate attribute understood apply throughout source polygon. rules encode different assumptions. Area weighting account within-polygon population distribution, land use, spatial heterogeneity unless information supplied separately.

text: Line geometries support total length metres, length density, distinct feature counts, presence.
code: roads <- sf::st_sf(   road_id = 1:2,   geometry = sf::st_sfc(     sf::st_linestring(matrix(c(8, 48, 14, 52), ncol = 2, byrow = TRUE)),     sf::st_linestring(matrix(c(18, 58, 23, 62), ncol = 2, byrow = TRUE)),     crs = 4326   ) )  road_length <- pg_from_vector(   x = roads,   variable = "road_length_m",   aggregation = "length",   config = config )  head(road_length) #>   pgid road_length_m #> 1  487     217419.95 #> 2  488      90616.64 #> 3  524     534502.68 #> 4  525      35523.43 #> 5  561     263563.13

title: Converting vector data
text: Polygon rules include area, cell coverage, feature count, presence, ordinary value summaries, area-weighted means, area-weighted allocation totals. Use weighted_mean overlap areas weight rate continuous attribute. Use weighted_sum allocate source polygon total proportion overlap cell.
code: region <- sf::st_polygon(list(matrix(   c(5, 45, 15, 45, 15, 55, 5, 55, 5, 45),   ncol = 2,   byrow = TRUE ))) regions <- sf::st_sf(value = 100, geometry = sf::st_sfc(region, crs = 4326))  coverage <- pg_from_vector(   x = regions,   variable = "region_coverage",   aggregation = "coverage",   config = config )  head(coverage) #>   pgid region_coverage #> 1  487       0.2390021 #> 2  488       0.2390021 #> 3  523       0.2656660 #> 4  524       0.2656660

text: priogridR provides consistent interface working PRIO-GRID data. combines grid utilities general converters transfer raster, vector, point-event, NetCDF, geographically indexed tabular data configurable PRIO-GRID. package builds official priogrid package grid definitions raster transformations.

title: Functions for Working with PRIO-GRID Data
text: user-facing functions begin pg_ use snake case: pg_from_raster() converts raster layers. pg_from_vector() converts point, line, polygon features. pg_from_points() convenience wrapper event coordinate data. pg_from_netcdf() converts NetCDF variables layers. pg_from_table() transfers geographically indexed tabular data. pg_create_indices() creates PRIO-GRID identifier matrices. pg_neighbors() returns first-order neighboring cells. pg_paths() constructs reproducible project paths. pg_theme() supplies map-oriented ggplot2 theme. pg_write_result() writes conversion outputs.

title: Functions for Working with PRIO-GRID Data
text: Point-event data can aggregated using temporal spatial settings PRIO-GRID configuration: See vignette("getting-started", package = "priogridR") vignette("conversion-workflows", package = "priogridR") introduction guide choosing converter. package website also provides focused article every pg_from_*() function.
code: library(priogridR)  pg_create_indices(nrow = 3, ncol = 3) pg_neighbors(5, nrow = 3, ncol = 3) events <- data.frame(   longitude = c(10, 10.1, 20),   latitude = c(50, 50.1, 60),   event_date = as.Date(c("2020-01-01", "2020-03-01", "2021-06-01")) )  config <- priogrid::pg_config(   temporal_resolution = "1 year",   start_date = as.Date("2020-12-31"),   end_date = as.Date("2021-12-31") )  event_counts <- pg_from_points(   x = events,   variable = "event_count",   longitude = "longitude",   latitude = "latitude",   aggregation = "count",   time_column = "event_date",   config = config )
